text:
jia: heads-up, APAC pool5 is showing a sustained ECC correctable spike on GPU cards (started ~14:11 UTC). rate ~0.8/sec on a few nodes. not full Xid floods yet but trend looks bad. logs attached below.

matt: can you paste the node IDs? are these the older A100s in pool5?

jia: node ids: apac-pool5-n{12,13,19}. models impacted are mostly short-context chat routes. sample syslog: ```
Mar 17 14:12:03 apac-pool5-n12 kernel: [GPU] ECC_CORRECTABLE: gpu=GPU0 addr=0x7f8d8 Xid=13 pcie_reset=1
Mar 17 14:12:04 apac-pool5-n12 runtime: warn: kv-cache miss high, batching fallback
Mar 17 14:12:05 apac-pool5-n13 kernel: [GPU] ECC_CORRECTABLE: gpu=GPU1 addr=0x9abf Xid=13 pcie_link_down=1
```

anika: thanks. what's current auto-drain threshold? I thought we were at 5 correctables/min per card for soft-drain?

kevin: our policy is 300/min per node aggregated across cards, plus 10/min per card for hard-evac. but APAC has low spare so we usually soft-drain earlier to avoid noisy evicts.

ops-bot: ALERT: ecc-rate(apac-pool5) = 48/min last 5m; threshold_soft=30/min; threshold_hard=600/min

matt: interesting — ops-bot thinks soft threshold crossed. but earlier in pool5 we saw lots of transient bursts that self-resolved after PCIe resets. auto-drain caused capacity crunch last month. we need to avoid cascading removes.

jia: agreed. request: propose a short-lived "soft-quarantine" state: remove node from scheduler placement, but keep existing containers and only schedule evacuation during maintenance window or if hard threshold hit. reduces flapping and eviction churn.

anika: that could help. alternative is to raise soft threshold for APAC pools to 45/min and add a 10m suppression window after first PCIe reset event to avoid immediate drain.

kevin: both options ok but we need telemetry first. can we enhance metrics to attribute ECC spikes to PCIe resets vs memory-only correctables? if it's link-related, quick link retrain seems to fix.

jia: I ran a correlation over last 90d: ~65% of Xid13 bursts in APAC coincide with PCIe link events within 30s. sample query: ```promql
sum(rate(gpu_ecc_correctable_total{region="apac",pool="pool5"}[5m])) by (node)
```

matt: good data. proposal: 1) implement soft-quarantine (scheduler-level cordon) as interim, 2) bump APAC soft threshold to 45/min and add 10m suppression after PCIe reset event, 3) add metric gpu_pcie_link_flap_total and alert when link_flap_rate > 1/min.

anika: +1 to experiment. add a runbook: if quarantine triggered, SRE should check link logs, attempt remote link retrain (ipmitool or driver), and if persistent >1h escalate to replacement. keep owners: oncall->eng-infra->hw-ops.

kevin: we should also prevent auto-evac during business hours for APAC until experiment done. schedule soft-evac window in off-peak (02:00-05:00 local).

ops-bot: NOTE: created incident ticket INFRA-APAC-2034 for spike & follow-up (assigned to @jia).

jia: I'll own the runbook and add the quarantine flag in the scheduler PR today. will also add the prom metric for link_flap and the suppression logic.

matt: thanks. one more ask — add a short meta-tag on quarantined nodes: "quarantine:reason=ecc-pcie-flap" so future automation can prefer warm-failover instead of immediate evict.

anika: agreed. also please add cost note in the ticket: previous month we lost ~4% capacity for 12h due to cascade drains in APAC (loss ~ $X). want exec visibility if this experiment risks short-term capacity loss.

kevin: +1. i'll draft an email to growth ops with the estimated impact and mitigation plan.

sre-bot: REMINDER: follow-up review scheduled in 72h for INFRA-APAC-2034.

jia: action items: (1) PR for soft-quarantine + tag (2) Prom rule for link_flap + suppression (3) bump soft threshold for APAC pool to 45/min (4) update runbook and maintenance window. I'll link PRs in the ticket.

matt: sounds good. :thumbsup:

anika: thanks team, keep logs and traces in the ticket. if we see hard threshold or Xid floods we still auto-evac immediately.

kevin: logging note — include lspci output, dmesg and driver version in the runbook so hw-ops can triage quickly.

jia: will do. updating ticket now.

matt: closing the thread here, monitor for next 6h, if spike continues escalate. :eyes:
